construct: When renal perfusion is reduced, angiotensin II constricts efferent arterioles to support glomerular capillary pressure. ACE inhibition removes this compensatory efferent constriction, lowering intraglomerular pressure and GFR.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: In bilateral renal artery stenosis, GFR depends strongly on angiotensin II-mediated efferent constriction. ACE inhibition removes this support, dilates the efferent arteriole, and lowers glomerular capillary pressure.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: ACE inhibitors also reduce systemic arterial pressure, which can affect filtration, but in bilateral renal artery stenosis the high-yield direct intrarenal mechanism is loss of angiotensin II-mediated efferent tone with reduced glomerular capillary pressure.
